summary: Khenpo Dazer worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and held teaching posts at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and Shri Singha Shedra.

Khenpo Gangshar was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shechen Monastery (~1937–1950) under Khyentse Ozer, Shyé Chen Kong Trul Pema Drimé, and Karsé Kongtrul, later serving as senior teacher there (~1950–1957).

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok studied under Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel (~1947–1951), Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima (~1951–1957), Yonten Gonpo, Khenchen Dazer, and several other teachers.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1958) and under the 8th Traleg Rinpoche, Khenpo Gangshar, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He taught at Rumtek Monastery and became abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra in 1978.
Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen Rinpoche is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.
Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö works in the fields of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Bokar Rinpoche.
Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.

Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied under Önpo Tenzin Norbu, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and others. He taught at Shri Singha Shedra from 1902 and became the first khenpo of Dzongsar Monastery's shedra in 1918.
Khenpo Sherab Püntsok studied under Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

A scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He became principal teacher at Rumtek Monastery's shedra (~1977) and spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery in 1992.
Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel and Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok (~1984–2004).

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under Shukseb Jetsun Choying Zangmo, Dudjom Rinpoche, and others. He taught at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (1960–1970) and at the University of Virginia (~1980–1981).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, he studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das, Dev Narayan Tripathi, and others. He held teaching posts at Lhasa Mentsikhang and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Active in Tibetology, Khyenrab Norbu studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen.
Ki-yong Rhi was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and as professor emeritus in 2007.

Kiattisak Ponampon is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Otago, supervised by Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie. He also studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and others in 2013.

A philosopher, Ito studied at the First Higher School, University of Tokyo, and University of Freiburg. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1911–1918, 1923–1945), served as dean at Hokkaido University (1947, 1950–1951), and was professor at Chuo University (1951–1958).
Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and religious studies. She completed a PhD at Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott works in religious studies and Indology. She held posts at the University of Leeds (~1984–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012).

Kim Plofker specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Haverford College and Brown University under David Pingree. Her posts include Brown, MIT, Utrecht University, and Union College, where she became Associate Professor in 2019.
